idiom_name: Enumerable#each / Thread fan-out over recipient objects
implementation_notes: Ruby has no messaging framework in the standard library, but the structure reduces to data plus Enumerable: the recipient set is an Array resolved per message whose elements respond to deliver, and recipients.each { |r| r.deliver(msg.dup) } is the entire fan-out in one line; for overlap, map to Thread.new and join, or use Concurrent::Promises from concurrent-ruby for a bounded pool and future-style combinators. The language form - a loop over data - is what replaces the classic router class, so an explicit RecipientList object only earns its place when resolution rules or failure policy must be shared. Brokers and job runners (Bunny, Sidekiq) add durability without changing the shape above.
code_sketch:
recipients = RecipientRegistry.for(msg)      # data-driven recipient set
threads = recipients.map do |recipient|
  Thread.new { recipient.deliver(msg.dup) }  # own copy per recipient
end
threads.each(&:join)                         # wait for every delivery
pitfalls: MRI's GVL means threads only overlap I/O; CPU-bound fan-out needs processes (fork, Ractors), and an unbounded Thread.new per recipient per message is a resource leak.
An exception inside a thread kills only that thread and stays silent until someone calls join or value, so delivery failures must be rescued and recorded explicitly.
Threads that are never joined and not referenced can be reaped at process exit mid-send; keep the thread array alive until the fan-out completes.
